title: A localization has the square-zero lifting property (is formally smooth)
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $W\subseteq R$ a multiplicative subset ($1\in W$, $st\in W$ for $s,t\in W$) and $\lambda:R\to R'$ a localization of $R$ at $W$: (a) $\lambda(s)$ is a unit of $R'$ for every $s\in W$; (b) every element of $R'$ is $\lambda(r)\lambda(s)^{-1}$ for some $r\in R$, $s\in W$; (c) $\lambda(r)=0$ implies $sr=0$ for some $s\in W$ (for instance $R'=W^{-1}R$, the ring of fractions, with $r\mapsto r/1$); $R'$ is an $R$-algebra via $\lambda$. Let $D$ be an $R$-algebra, $N\subseteq D$ an ideal with $N^2=0$ and $q:D\to D/N$ the quotient map [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Then for every homomorphism of $R$-algebras $g:R'\to D/N$ there is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $f:R'\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$.
